compliance.emc: FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; CAN ICES-003 (A)/NMB-003(A); CISPR 32 Class A; VCCI Class A
compliance.installation: suitable for Information Technology Rooms per NEC Article 645 and NFPA 75
compliance.nebs: NEBS statements only, not a stated certification level: suitable for installation as part of the Common Bonding Network (CBN); installable in Network Telecommunications Facilities where the National Electric Code applies; DC input terminals are DC-I (isolated DC return) and the RTN terminal is to be isolated from the chassis or rack; the intra-building OOB Ethernet port is for unexposed intra-building wiring only (GR-1089 Type 2, 4 or 4a) and must not be metallically connected to OSP wiring for more than 6 m. An external Surge Protection Device must be used with AC powered equipment, installed at the AC service entrance.
compliance.safety: IEC/EN 60825-1 laser Class 1 pluggables only (UL/CSA recognised modules); installation restricted to service personnel, indoors only

environmental.altitude: rated for operation up to 5000 m (HIG Connecting Power, both input types)

features.gnss: internal receiver for master clock implementations - GPS/QZSS L1 C/A, GLONASS L1OF, BeiDou B1, SBAS L1 C/A (WAAS, EGNOS, MSAS, GAGAN), Galileo E1B/C; minimum RF sensitivity -166 dBm, and the port supplies up to 5 V DC / 150 mA to an active antenna
features.gnss-exclusivity: the platform supports either GNSS or SMA-10MHz input at a time; the 10MHz input is disabled when the GNSS antenna is connected (HIG section 12)
features.nos: NOS integration is necessary to activate the timing features
features.optics-qsfp28: 100G QSFP28 SR4, LR4, ER4, ZR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver types)
features.optics-qsfp56: 200G QSFP56 SR4, FR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver types; the QSFP56 cages also take the QSFP28 optics at 40/100G)
features.optics-sfp-plus: 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER (datasheet compatible transceiver types; the two 10G management ports take the same optics as the SFP28 cages do at 10G)
features.optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR, LR, ER; 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER; 1G SFP SX, LX, EX (datasheet compatible transceiver types)
features.routing: full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6); programmable as a Broadband Network Gateway
features.timing: Stratum 3E OCXO, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (G.8265.1 default, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with additional licence; T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC), Time Sensitive Networking, ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C accuracy, IEEE 802.1CM
features.timing-cables: 50 ohm SMA coax with 1/4-36UNS-2B for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coax with 10-32UNF-2A for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD, 3 m maximum
features.timing-interfaces: GNSS SMA in, 1PPS SMB in/out, 10MHz SMB in/out, ToD RJ45 in/out

management.boot-time: approx 80 s from power-on under Ubuntu Linux; OOB Ethernet relinks in approx 40 s (HIG NEBS statements, both qualified as NOS-dependent)

power.input-dc: -48 to -60 VDC, 37 A max per supply
power.pdu-fuse-suggested: 30 A DC, 15 A AC (HIG provisioning guidance, not a draw)
power.power-max-w-ac: 808 (HIG AC section; the DC build's 811 is the figure carried as power-max-w)

thermal.fans: 4x hot-swappable 3+1 redundant, exhaust airflow; system front-to-back

gaps.note: The badge printed at the bottom right of the faceplate reads S9600-104BC in HIG Figure 8 at 600 dpi - five glyphs before the hyphen, the last of them a round 0 the same width as the one before it, against an unmistakably narrow 1 after the hyphen. No UfiSpace product is called S9600-104BC. The guide, the datasheet and the product page all title the unit S9601-104BC, so the badge is drawn S9601-104BC and this entry records that the only legible rendering of it says otherwise. The two vendor photographs are 520 and 650 px wide and cannot resolve the character.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution front photograph of the badge, or the unit

gaps.note: The QSFP block sits between two perforated plates, and each is magenta over the left-hand column and green over the right-hand one. By position the magenta half covers the QSFP28 ports and the green half the QSFP56 ports, which is exactly what a media colour code looks like - but the plate appears in no callout, no table and no procedure, and nothing in either document mentions a colour convention. It is drawn as vent-patterned panel decor because that is what it looks like; if it is in fact part of the QSFP cage assembly it belongs in a component instead, and if the colours do encode media then the boundary belongs on the cage-column line at 412.5 rather than at the 414.2 where it is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace exploded view, a close photograph of the QSFP block, or any vendor statement about the colour code

gaps.note: The SFP28 blocks print their port numbers on the yellow and cream bands and those are transcribed. The QSFP block has no such band - the coloured plates occupy that space - and no printed numeral is legible on it at the only resolution available. Ports 96-103 are numbered here from the HIG's Port Overview table and from Figure 8's large annotation overlay, which is the figure's own labelling rather than the panel's ink, so no silkscreen mark is written for them.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution front photograph, or a vendor 3D model

gaps.note: The land between each QSFP pair carries a dot matrix that resolves as dots but not as countable rows and not as wiring. The upper strip is assigned to the upper port and the lower strip to the lower port BY POSITION ONLY; the HIG tables no port lamp of any kind. ufispace/lane-led-quad's four lamps are taken as the arrangement because that component was built for this vendor's QSFP blocks, not because four were counted here.
gaps.wanted: a lit-unit photograph, or a UfiSpace port-LED table

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six system lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The ninety-eight arrow lamps, eight lane-lamp strips and two management-jack lamps therefore keep their component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Unlike the S9510-28DC's tables, not one row here is annotated 'need NOS to activate', so there is no evidence either way about whether these are NOS-defined.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: A two-high ganged SFP block normally mirrors so that both rows' bail latches stay reachable, and std/sfp-ganged draws an asymmetric aperture that would show it. The only elevation that resolves these cages is HIG Figure 8, and Figure 8 prints its large annotation numerals ON the cages, covering exactly the detail that would settle it. The rows are drawn belly-to-belly, the lower row rotate 180, because the port lamps between the rows point up over down and that is the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3: upper rotate 0 over lower 180, both bails outward) - lamps and the rule, not a measurement of the metal.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution front photograph, or a vendor 3D model

gaps.note: Two UfiSpace hardware guides give the same ordering name two different faces. This device's HIG tables 'Fan (W x D x H) 81*138.80*81.5mm' and its datasheet orders 'FAN-803816-HI'; the S9600-28DX HIG tables that same part number at '80 x 113 x 81.5mm'. Width 81 against 80 and depth 138.8 against 113 - the depths differ by 23 percent, which is more than a rounding, so these may be two builds sharing an ordering name. The bays here are drawn 81.0 x 81.5 from THIS device's own table and seat ufispace/fan-808012@1, whose contract is exactly that face; the part number FAN-803816-HI is carried in the configurations. ufispace/fan-803816-hi@1 exists in the library at 80.0 x 81.5 and is deliberately not used here.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan FRU datasheet, or a photograph of the module's own label

gaps.note: The datasheet prints a REGULATORY COMPLIANCE block with the headings Safety, EMC and Environment and NOTHING under any of them. This was confirmed by rendering page 2 at 600 dpi and looking at it, not only by extracting the text, because outlined glyphs would look the same to an extractor - the block is genuinely blank. Every compliance value carried here therefore comes from HIG section 13, which gives FCC, ICES, CISPR, VCCI and NEBS statements but names no safety standard beyond the laser class and no environmental directive at all. In particular there is NO UL 62368-1 or IEC 62368-1 claim in the intake for this model, and none is inferred from the sibling S9600-102XC.
gaps.wanted: a revision of the datasheet with the compliance block filled in, or a UfiSpace declaration of conformity

gaps.note: ufispace/fan-808012 states no draw and its own contract records the search. This HIG is the same - it weighs the fan FRU at 1.14 lb (520 g) and tables its lamp, and its only wattages are the two system maxima (811 W DC, 808 W AC), the 1300 W per-circuit reserve and the PDU fuse suggestions, none of which is a fan's draw. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis module total is a floor. With four fans in a 2RU 104-port chassis this is a material hole, not a rounding one.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet

gaps.note: No figure or photograph in the intake shows a flank square-on. The five rail attachment pins per side and the single M4 locking screw per side are drawn because HIG section 5 states their count and says the locking screw is at the front, but their heights and pitch are estimated. The isometric photograph shows a flank foreshortened and confirms that the pins exist and that the face is otherwise plain metal; it cannot be measured.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing or an orthographic side elevation

gaps.note: The upper coloured plate is cleanly bounded at y 7.6-11.5 and x 392.4-435.0. The lower one sits at y 75.6-79.6 where it overlaps the bottom perforated field, and its right edge could not be separated from that field by colour; it is drawn the same width as the upper plate on the assumption that they are a pair, which the figure supports visually and does not resolve.

gaps.wanted: a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, qsfp56, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

attrs.note: datasheet (Physical / Environmental / Performance) and HIG (the Port Overview table for reach and speed, section 11 for the console settings, section 12 for the GNSS receiver's frequencies and antenna requirements, section 13 for compliance). THE DATASHEET'S REGULATORY COMPLIANCE BLOCK IS EMPTY IN THIS REVISION - the headings Safety, EMC and Environment are printed with nothing under any of them, confirmed by rendering page 2 at 600 dpi and looking, not only by extracting its text - so every compliance value here comes from HIG section 13 and is transcribed as printed. See the datasheet-compliance-empty gap.

bottom.note: estimated - no source in the intake shows the underside. The compliance sticker is the house convention at an estimated position. A bottom view mirrors LEFT and RIGHT; the sticker is the only content, so the axis was checked and does not bite.

chassis.note: datasheet '2 RU, 440 x 440 x 87.7 mm or 17.32" x 17.32" x 3.45"', 'Weight: 14.73kg or 32.47lb (without FRU)', with the HIG's Component Physical Information table repeating both to the same precision ('S9601-104BC (W x D x H) 17.32 x 17.32 x 3.45 in (440 x 440 x 87.7mm)', 'Chassis without FRU 32.47.49lb (14.73kg)' - the weight cell has a typo in the pound figure and the kilogram figure is used). 440 IS THE BODY, NOT THE RACK FACE: the HIG's Space Clearance section says 'The S9601-104BC width is 17.32 inches (44.0cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks'. The brackets are visible in Figure 8 as tabs beyond both ends of the face and are not drawn. Depth 440 is likewise 'without the field replaceable units (FRUs)'; Space Clearance adds that the fan handle stands 29 mm proud and the PSU handle 30 mm, and asks for 6 inches of clearance at each end.

front-figure-scale.note: drawing - HIG page 12, the Figure 8 port-overview elevation, re-rendered at 600 dpi. GATE 1: the drawn faceplate measures 3636 x 724 px (x 904.5-4540.5, y 1973.3-2697.5), which is 8.264 px/mm against 440 mm and 8.255 px/mm against 87.7 mm - 0.1% apart. The figure is orthographic and every front coordinate below is measured on it at 8.2636 px/mm. TWO EDGES HAVE TO BE EXCLUDED OR THE GATE FAILS: the caption rule 88 px below the panel, and the rack-mount ear tabs that stick out past both ends at the top and bottom of the face (x 885-904 and 4541-4559, about 100 px tall against the panel's 724). Neither is metal between the ear folds.

fru-components.note: reuses ufispace/fan-808012 and adds two new supplies, and the match is dimensional rather than nominal in both directions. FANS: this HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the fan an 81 x 138.80 x 81.5 mm envelope, so the face is 81.0 x 81.5, which is exactly ufispace/fan-808012's contract size; ufispace/fan-803816-hi carries the part number this datasheet orders (FAN-803816-HI) but a face of 80.0 x 81.5, taken from the S9600-28DX HIG's table for the same part number. Two UfiSpace guides therefore give the same ordering name two widths a millimetre apart - recorded as the fan-face-width gap - and the component that matches THIS device's own table is the one seated, with the part number carried in the configurations' component-attrs where a FRU model belongs. That is the same treatment, for the same split, as ufispace/s9600-102xc. SUPPLIES: none of the ten existing ufispace/psu-* contracts fits. The 1300 W parts in the library (psu-132-ac, psu-132-dc) are 50.5 x 40 faces from a 321 mm-long supply; the 73.5 x 40 faces in the library (psu-242-*) are 2400 W CRPS units with a C20 inlet. This chassis wants a 1300 W supply on a 73.5 x 40 CRPS face with a C14 inlet, so ufispace/psu-132-crps-ac and ufispace/psu-132-crps-dc were built for it.

led-semantics.note: HIG section 10, pages 22-23, transcribed rather than only cited. The Front Panel LED table is the S9600-102XC's six-lamp table (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID) with the same states, and the PSU FRU and Fan FRU tables belong to the modules and are transcribed in ufispace/psu-132-crps-ac, psu-132-crps-dc and ufispace/fan-808012. Not one row anywhere in this guide is annotated 'need NOS to activate', unlike the S9510-28DC's, so there is no evidence either way about NOS dependence.

left.note: drawing-fraction and estimated. HIG section 5's rack-mounting text is the only source that says anything about a flank: 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' for the inner rail, plus 'two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)'. Five pins per side are drawn on an even pitch across the depth at an estimated height, because no figure in the intake shows a flank square-on and nothing dimensions them. AXIS: x = 0 is the REAR on a left view (viewer3d.js convention). This face carries only content that is symmetric front to back apart from the locking screw, which HIG section 5 places 'at the front of the chassis' - so the axis is load-bearing here and was checked rather than happening not to matter.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9601-104BC end of life end of sale' - no announcement found; the product page is live and the unit is actively distributed (EPS Global lists it). none-announced is a real finding, not an omission.

mgmt-cluster.note: drawing-measured - one silver bezel at x 24.26-39.99, y 49.34-80.44 holding three things in a column, measured by scanning down its middle: the out-of-band RJ45 (drawn face x 26.08-38.30, y 50.43-60.11, with green link lamps in its TOP corners so it is keyway-up and rotated 180), a USB 3.0 Type-A socket whose blue tongue measures x 27.41-37.57 y 63.37-64.83 - the datasheet's '1 x USB 3.0 Type-A port', and the HIG calls it 'a maintenance port' - and the RS-232 console RJ45 keyway-down at y 70.03-78.62, labelled IOIOI below at y 82.7-83.6, which is the HIG's own spelling ('The console can be connected with the IOIO port'). Both RJ45s are std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11): the bezel is 15.7 wide and 31.1 tall, which will not take two 16 x 14 IEC cutouts and a USB. Three icons are printed above the bezel at y 44.4-47.4 - a network glyph at x 23.9-26.6, an up/down arrow pair at 28.7-33.6 and the USB SuperSpeed trident at 35.2-37.2. The recessed RESET button is a ring centred (16.76, 46.74) about 2.5 mm across, drawn with common/reset-button at its own 4.0 contract size, with RESET printed under it.

mgmt-sfp-plus.note: drawing-measured - the two 10G SFP+ management ports are a one-column, two-row ganged block of their own at x 27.5-43.6, y 15.6-41.6, sharing the upper blocks' rows exactly (cage aperture measured 28.50-42.54 across at y 19-24, and the block has the same two-row-plus-land structure). Cage at x 28.45. It carries no yellow band; its '0 up down 1' legend is printed white on the bare faceplate above it at y 12.7-14.7, with the two triangles measured at x 32.6 and 38.3. The vendor numbers these ports 0 and 1 in their own sequence, which is why they are a separate group: the traffic ports also start at 0.

model-badge.note: THE FIGURE'S OWN BADGE READS S9600-104BC AND THE MODEL IS DRAWN S9601-104BC. At 600 dpi the badge at x 346-364, y 81.7-83.9 resolves letter by letter as S 9 6 0 0 - 1 0 4 B C: the character after the hyphen is unmistakably a narrow 1 and the fifth character before it is a round 0 the same width as the fourth. S9600-104BC names no UfiSpace product - the S9600 series is the 102XC, 28DX, 32X, 56DX, 64X and 72XC - while the guide is titled S9601-104BC on every page, the datasheet is titled S9601-104BC and the product page is S9601-104BC. Printing the badge as drawn would put a model that does not exist on the chassis, so the badge is drawn with the model both documents title and the discrepancy is filed as the model-badge gap rather than silently corrected.

port-pitch.note: drawing-measured, AND MEASURED FROM FEATURES THAT REPEAT ONCE PER PORT rather than from the filled rectangles the figure draws for the module faces. Three independent per-port rulers agree. (1) The bright vertical separator lines between cages in the upper-left block fall at 45.62, 59.96, 74.18, 88.52, 102.62, 131.12, 145.22, 159.37, 202.09 and 216.49 - eight interior lines plus both block edges, spanning twelve columns in 170.87, a pitch of 14.239. (2) The same lines in the right-hand block run 219.46, 234.04, 248.50, 262.60, 276.76, 291.04, 305.25, 319.41, 333.57, 347.97, 362.07, 376.23 - eleven intervals in 156.77, a pitch of 14.252. (3) The black up/down arrow pairs printed on the yellow band repeat at 14.222. 14.25 mm is also exactly std/sfp-ganged's contract width (SFF-8433 port pitch B04), so the standard part fits with no gutter, and 14.25 is what is used. ONE THING IN THE FIGURE DISAGREES AND IS NOT FOLLOWED: the black vertical divider the figure draws between the two blocks occupies x 219.7-221.5, which overlaps the right-hand block's first cage by 1.7 mm. The lattice is fixed by eleven intervals of a repeated feature and the divider by one drawn bar, so the lattice wins and the divider here is the 1.1 mm gap the two block shells leave between them.

power.note: three figures, two measures, no conflict. The datasheet's Environmental block gives 'Typical power: 282.2 Watts (no transceiver)' - a typical, explicitly with the cages empty, which on a 104-port box is a large qualifier. The HIG's Connecting Power section gives a maximum twice, once per input type: 'The maximum system power consumption is 811 watts' in the DC section and '808 watts' in the AC section. Those are not two readings of one number - they are the same measure of two different builds, three watts apart, and 811 is recorded as power-max-w because it is the higher and the one a budget has to carry, with the AC figure named here. NEITHER MAXIMUM IS QUALIFIED - no ambient, no optics population, no traffic load - so power-envelope is 'unstated' rather than 'bare': the typical declares its scope and the maxima do not, and no single envelope word covers both. The suggested PDU fuse ratings (30 A DC, 15 A AC) and the 1300 W per-circuit reserve are provisioning instructions and PSU nameplates respectively, not draws, and are not recorded as any. Per-PSU rating lives on the ufispace/psu-132-crps-* contracts.

qsfp-blocks.note: drawing-measured - EIGHT QSFP cages in two blocks of two columns by two rows, not six as on the S9600-102XC. Cage columns at x 393.7 and 412.8, from bright separators at 393.59, 412.77 and 431.53, a 19.1 mm pitch against std/qsfp-ganged's 18.5 contract width so the cages do not abut. The rows are CENTRED ON THE SFP ROWS: the land between the QSFP rows reads 25.98-32.27 and 55.51-62.41, the same lands as the SFP blocks to a tenth, so the QSFP cages sit at y 16.71 / 31.51 and 46.81 / 61.61, each 9.58 tall and on the same row centres as their SFP neighbours. Port identity is the HIG Port Overview table read against Figure 8's own numerals: the LEFT column is 96 over 97 and 100 over 101, all QSFP28; the RIGHT column is 98 over 99 and 102 over 103, all QSFP56. ALL EIGHT ARE DRAWN WITH std/qsfp-ganged, INCLUDING THE FOUR QSFP56: std/qsfp56 is 20.0 wide and cannot sit on a 19.1 mm measured pitch, and its own provenance says that 20.0 is 'assumed = QSFP28 bezel opening' while qsfp-ganged's 18.5 is measured off a real ganged cage. The right pitch beats the right name here, and the media is carried by the group rather than by the part.

qsfp-lamps.note: drawing-measured - the land between each QSFP pair carries a dense dot matrix rather than the SFP blocks' two arrows. At 8.26 px/mm it resolves as dots but not as rows that can be counted with confidence, so ufispace/lane-led-quad (14.4 x 2.6, four round lamps on a 3.94 pitch, built for this vendor's QSFP blocks) is used, one strip per port, stacked in the land at y 26.3 and 29.3 (upper) and 56.2 and 59.2 (lower), inset 2.05 mm from each cage's left edge so the strip is centred in the 18.5 mm column. WHICH STRIP SERVES WHICH PORT IS BY POSITION ONLY - see the qsfp-lane-lamp-ownership gap.

qsfp-plate.note: drawing-measured - the QSFP block sits between two perforated plates, one above (y 7.6-11.5) and one below (y 75.6-79.6), and EACH PLATE IS TWO COLOURS: magenta from x 392.4 to 414.2 and green from 414.2 to 435.0, sampled at #623a46 and #365927 in the figure and drawn a little brighter here so they read at faceplate scale. By position the magenta half sits over the QSFP28 column and the green half over the QSFP56 column, which is what a media colour code would look like - but no document says so, and the colour boundary reads 414.2 against a cage-column boundary at 412.5, so the two are drawn where they were measured rather than reconciled. See the qsfp-plate gap.

rear.note: drawing-measured, and this rear figure PASSES the aspect gate where the S9600-102XC's did not. HIG page 10, Figure 4's rear elevation re-rendered at 600 dpi: the body measures 1591 x 323 px, and the two scales are settled by two features of KNOWN size rather than by the outline. The PSU face is tabled 73.5 x 40 and measures 263 x 145 px, giving 3.578 and 3.625 px/mm; the outline would give 3.616 across and 3.683 down. 3.6159 px/mm is used on both axes, which is the width scale, and it puts the PSU within 0.4 percent on both of its own axes while the height scale would put it 2 percent out. The 6 px the height then over-runs is the drawn outline stroke. Fan bays at x 4.4 / 88.4 / 172.4 / 256.4, from bright seams measured at 4.4, 88.6, 173.4 and 257.0 and evened to an 84.0 mm pitch - the scatter is +/- 0.6 mm, which is two pixels, and an uneven fan row is a failed measurement rather than a finding. THAT 84.0 PITCH IS INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME as the 84.2 and 84.1 two other UfiSpace chassis already use for this fan (ufispace/s9600-102xc and ufispace/fan-803816-hi's own provenance), which is corroboration and not a borrowed number. PSUs stacked at x 350.9, y 2.8 and 46.2, size 73.5 x 40 from the HIG table and confirmed on the figure. The narrow strip right of the supplies carries, top to bottom, PSU0, an earth symbol with the grounding studs at the chassis edge beside it, 0123 over FAN, and PSU1.

rear-fan-height.note: THE TABLE AND THE FIGURE DISAGREE ABOUT THE FAN AND THE TABLE IS FOLLOWED. The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives 'Fan (W x D x H) 81*138.80*81.5mm', so the face is 81.0 x 81.5 and the bays are drawn that size, centred vertically at y 3.1. Figure 4 draws the fan face filling the chassis height, y 0.3 to 87.7 at the scale above - 87.4 mm, six millimetres more than the table. The two are the module envelope and the bezel flange in its slot, the same disagreement ufispace/fan-803816-hi records for its own family, and the table wins for size.

right.note: drawing-fraction and estimated - the mirror of the left, and deliberately the same content, because the guide describes the two sides identically ('one on each chassis side'). THE GROUNDING POINT IS NOT ON A FLANK ON THIS CHASSIS: HIG section 8 says 'The location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label', and Figure 4's rear elevation prints the earth symbol on the strip right of the supplies, so both flanks are plain. AXIS: x = 0 is the FRONT on a right view, so the locking screw sits at the opposite end of this face from where it sits on the left one.

sfp28-blocks.note: drawing-measured - the 96 SFP28 ports are FOUR blocks of twelve columns by two rows, not one field: an upper pair at x 45.6-216.6 and 219.5-390.5, and a lower pair on the same two x ranges. NUMBERING RUNS DOWN COLUMNS AND ACROSS BLOCKS: 0-23 upper-left, 24-47 upper-right, 48-71 lower-left, 72-95 lower-right, even on the top row of each, which is what Figure 8's own numerals show. Rows measured from the drawn module faces at 17.39-25.62 and 32.27-40.38 (upper) and 47.40-55.87 and 62.41-70.51 (lower); the port OPENING is 10.4 tall against that 8.2 mm face, so the cages sit at y 16.3 / 31.1 and 46.4 / 61.2 - a 14.8 mm row pitch within a block and 30.1 between them. The whole port field is ONE continuous light shell per block from y 11.8 to 77.6, not two shells with a dark gap: the band between the upper and lower rows reads #bdbfbc, the same grey as the cage rows, and never goes dark.

sfp28-lamps.note: drawing-measured - two pale arrow lamps per column in the light land between the rows, up serving the top (even) port and down the bottom (odd) one. Found as brightness minima across the land and reduced to offsets from the cage lattice: thirteen readings cluster at 5.14 (scatter 4.67-5.41) and thirteen at 8.85 (8.42-9.16), so the pair sits 3.71 mm apart. Land y 26.0-32.3 (upper) and 55.9-62.4 (lower) with the lamp centres at 28.75 and 58.75. Drawn with common/led-arrow-sm (2.25 x 2.0) rather than common/led-arrow (3.6 x 3.2), which would be twice the drawing's arrow and would fill the land; that choice, and the 3.70 mm pair separation it has to sit on, are the same as ufispace/s9600-102xc, which is the same vendor's same block idiom - but the 5.14 / 8.85 offsets here are measured on THIS figure and differ from that model's 5.60 / 9.30 by half a millimetre.

sfp28-legend.note: drawing-measured - each block carries one printed band on its OUTER edge: yellow above the upper blocks (y 12.1-15.7, #cccc4d) and cream below the lower ones (y 72.2-75.7, #d6d4c0). The band prints, per column, the even port number, a solid up triangle, a solid down triangle and the odd port number - the legend that says which of the two lamps in the central land belongs to which row. Measured against the cage lattice the even numeral starts at cage + 1.2 and the odd numeral ENDS at cage + 12.9, which is why they are anchored start and end rather than centred: single digits sit at 1.5 and 12.6 and two-digit numbers open at 1.5 and close at 12.5, so the numerals are edge-aligned and not centred. The triangles fall at cage + 5.6 and + 8.4. The numerals are transcribed here; the triangles are not, because they are a legend FOR the lamps and the lamps are modelled as parts.

sources.note: datasheet (s9601-104bc-datasheet.pdf, converted) and Hardware Installation Guide R1.7 (s9601-104bc-hig.pdf, converted, Figures 1-33), plus three vendor images: s9601-104bc-1-view.jpg (650x278, a three-quarter isometric), -2-view.jpg and -3-rear.jpg (both 520x150, front and rear elevations). ALL THREE PHOTOGRAPHS ARE TOO SMALL TO MEASURE - at 520 px across a 440 mm face they resolve 1.2 px/mm, so the 14.25 mm port pitch is seventeen pixels - and they were used for colour, counts and confirmation only. No mechanical drawing of the CHASSIS exists in the intake; there are mechanical drawings of the two power supplies (HIG Figures 5 and 6). Front, rear and top geometry comes from the HIG's own pages re-rendered at 600 dpi with pdftocairo, not from the extracted figure PNGs, which are the embedded rasters at their native resolution.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 49 SFP pairs (mport-0/mport-1 to port-94/port-95). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 4 QSFP pairs (port-96/port-97 to port-102/port-103).

status-leds.note: drawing-measured - six lamps in one column at x 14.82-17.85 (3.03 wide, 1.57 tall each) with tops at y 62.53, 64.95, 67.61, 70.03, 72.57 and 75.11, a mean pitch of 2.52 mm, and the legends printed dark on a white strip beside them at x 18.70-22.57 y 61.92-77.29. Order top to bottom SYNC SYS FAN PS0 PS1 ID, which is exactly the order of HIG section 10's Front Panel LED table; the bottom lamp is drawn blue in the figure and the table's only ID row is 'Blinking Blue - Beacon is enabled'. DRAWN WITH common/led-dot (2.0 x 2.0) ON THE MEASURED 2.52 PITCH, NOT WITH common/led-rect: led-rect is 4.6 x 2.6 and cannot sit on a 2.52 pitch without L13 firing, and stretching the column to fit it - which is what ufispace/s9600-102xc and ufispace/s9501-18smt did with their own tighter pitches - moves six lamps to keep one shape. The real lamp is a 3.0 x 1.6 rectangle and the dot is a compromise; the pitch is not.

timing-block.note: drawing-measured by colour (the three jacks are the only bright yellow features on the face). GNSS ANT centre (24.26, 7.71) and 9.56 mm across; 10MHZ centre (41.81, 7.71) and 7.14 across; 1PPS centre (59.18, 7.77) and 7.26 across. They run in a ROW along the top of the faceplate, as on the S9600-102XC and unlike the S9501-18SMT's column, and each label is printed to the LEFT of its jack - measured ends at 17.1, 37.1 and 53.5. The measured diameters confirm SMA, SMB, SMB and agree with common/sma-jack (9.5) and common/smb-jack (7.0) to within 0.26 mm; the components' own contract sizes are used, not the measurements. ToD is a single RJ45 low on the left, bezel measured x 9.14-24.51 y 28.52-41.47, a 15.5 x 13.1 bezel, which is the IEC 60603-7 single-port 16 x 14 cutout, so it is std/rj45 and not the ganged part.

top.note: drawing-measured, and the top view PASSES the aspect gate: HIG Figure 4's plan view measures 1355 x 1360 px for a body the same figure dimensions W = 17.32 in (440 mm) and D = 17.32 in (440 mm), which is 3.0795 and 3.0909 px/mm, 0.37 percent apart. AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and per the figure, which prints the fan handles at the top of the view. Three long recessed slots read at y 125.1-144.6, 230.1-249.6 and 335-355, spanning x 20 to 423. A row of three screws crosses at y 90 (x 110, 221, 331) and a second row runs along the front edge at y 429. Slot DEPTH is dimensioned nowhere and the sink value is estimated.

vents.note: drawing-measured by darkness - the faceplate carries a perforated field above and below the port shells. The top field runs y 1.9-11.4 and starts at x 65.5, just clear of the 1PPS jack; the bottom field runs y 77.9-82.8 from x 45. The left-hand service area has two smaller fields of its own, a single row of three holes at x 11.2-24.5 y 16.2-19.8 and a taller block at x 6.6-14.3 y 51.0-77.8 beside the status lamps. THE TWO MAIN FIELDS DO NOT REACH THE SAME LEFT EDGE and that asymmetry is what the figure draws: the top field is stopped by the timing jacks and the bottom one by the console bezel.
